contents: Equipment-reported yield and full-inspection good yield did not agree, so true process defects and inspection misclassification had to be separated under one basis. I aligned the yield denominator and measurement criteria, then managed owners, deadlines, local 4M+2E retests, and decision criteria on the same cells. I contributed to the team result of stabilizing monthly average good yield from about 40% to 98.7% and directly revised the MSA criteria, SOP, QCP, P-FMEA, and inspection standards.
summary: Equipment-reported yield and full-inspection good yield did not agree, so true process defects and inspection misclassification had to be separated under one basis. title: 2170 Assembly-Line Good-Yield Stabilization

contents: Product development and SAT were complete, but the actual new product was not reflected in laser, AI-vision, and X-ray conditions, while line interlocks and repeated motion remained dependent on manual operation and temporary recipes. As the lead engineering owner, I optimized three laser processes and rebuilt AI-vision, X-ray, Ready, measurement, and production standards for equipment with design constraints. Two 100-cell full-process lots and a final 50-cell continuous run validated the limited-production setup, followed by management approval and handoff of the field standards.
summary: Product development and SAT were complete, but the actual new product was not reflected in laser, AI-vision, and X-ray conditions, while line interlocks and repeated motion remained dependent on manual operation and temporary recipes. contents: A new cell with simultaneous changes in electrolyte, clad tabs, turn count, and can geometry had to be advanced on the existing 2170 line from PROTO through MP technical approval. I defined customer CTQs and changes, then led 4M risk analysis, Taguchi DOE, A/B/C sample trials, trial production, and customer qualification. Completed about 20,000-cell trial production and customer qualification/CCB.PO technical approval, with process, inspection, and production-handoff documents established.
summary: A new cell with simultaneous changes in electrolyte, clad tabs, turn count, and can geometry had to be advanced on the existing 2170 line from PROTO through MP technical approval. title: 25P LFP Power Cell DMADV and Taguchi NPI Process Development with Customer Qualification

contents: Without dedicated tabless equipment or jigs, existing 4695 equipment and manual work had to meet the safety and functional CTQs of a PROTO A sample. I defined objectives and measurements through DMADV, then compared jig, laser, and assembly factors selected through 4M in a Taguchi trial matrix while directly building and evaluating samples. Narrowed failure modes across about 100 trials and confirmed A-sample feasibility through Hi-Pot, IR, formation, capacity, and life evaluation on five functional samples.
summary: Without dedicated tabless equipment or jigs, existing 4695 equipment and manual work had to meet the safety and functional CTQs of a PROTO A sample. Narrowed failure modes across about 100 trials and confirmed A-sample feasibility through Hi-Pot, IR, formation, capacity, and life evaluation on five functional samples.
title: Next-Generation 2170 Tabless A-Sample Early Manufacturing Validation (PoC)

contents: Limited FAT samples and individual auto cycles could not prove site process handoffs, product quality, or production readiness. I defined specifications and acceptance sheets, led FAT/SAT and punch retests, and owned real-cell process, measurement, and early production operation. The team connected 11 core machines and 13 processes through about five days and 1,000 cells, observing about 95% initial assembly including reworked conforming cells and establishing operating standards.

contents: One incumbent can supplier could not cover planned volume alone, and alloy, thickness, tolerance, and burr differences had to be checked for assembly, sealing, welding, and vent-safety impact. As the lead process-validation engineer, I connected drawing/certificate and incoming review, beading/crimping/sizing/laser conditions, sample builds, sectioning, teardown, safety/performance tests, and field standards. Three 200-cell lots, 600 cells in total, and official UN38.3 passed, followed by a March 2025 transition of pilot production and purchase orders to the alternative can.

title: Cylindrical-Cell Alternative Can Supplier Qualification and Pilot Transition

contents: Tearing, active-material shedding, and shorts repeated after pre-welding, while manual pre-forming changed position and R shape by operator. I separated positive and negative damage mechanisms and owned the pilot-jig concept/drawing, geometry, position and acceptance criteria, sample/teardown tests, process documents, RFQ, and training. The basis was checked across about 200 initial disposable samples plus four lots of 50 and then used on subsequent samples, operator changes, and other sizes.

contents: Process MES records existed, but a cell's full history was not connected, so searching, matching, and organizing ten customer-requested cells took about three days. After a requested MES lookup enhancement did not proceed because of cost, I defined the relationships and built Power Query consolidation and Excel VBA search logic over about three weeks. Search took about 5–10 seconds per cell and about three minutes for ten cells; including report preparation it took about half a day, and the tool was used in the field and handed over.

contents: The new model lacked parts lists, assembly, and inspection standards, leaving latent risks of misalignment, vacuum leakage, loaded-motion alarms, and site-teaching error after assembly. I separated failure modes into 4M causes, preventive controls, and detection controls, then connected parts lists, SOPs, check sheets, FARO, helium leak, and loaded cycles in one overhaul control plan. At YMC, the work reached initial qualification and about five units of one model; at Bontech, it expanded into repeat overhaul, operator OJT, and domestic/overseas site setup.

title: Vacuum Transfer-Robot Overhaul Standard System and Field Setup

contents: A higher OLED process temperature exposed cracks and particles in a mixed-acid film for upper-electrode-type parts, while susceptor-type parts required a separate high-temperature qualification. Using a Six Sigma GB problem-solving sequence, I produced and evaluated samples, separated causes with 4M+2E, ran scale-up tests, and documented process and inspection criteria. The mixed-acid condition passed customer qualification and received about one year of additional follow-up; the oxalic-acid condition completed repeated 450℃ screening and customer vacuum-heat qualification before about one year of use.

title: High-Temperature Anodizing Development for Display Equipment Parts

I increased sampling to twice weekly and connected component-level analysis, external comparisons, and batch-test sample evaluation for Korea and China. The project standardized the analysis SOP, log sheet, replenishment/replacement decision, and product-sample checks for the target baths and China site.

contents: Internal process and inspection conditions did not match the global equipment maker's requirements, and matched-condition counterpart samples received different Hi-Pot decisions. I converted English specifications into process-level changes, reconfigured bead-blasting, oxalic-anodizing, and inspection conditions, and led Hi-Pot correlation and corrective audit retests. I aligned customer locations, seven repeats, voltage ramp, test sequence, and arc interpretation, closed one finding through three retests, and connected qualification to about one year of follow-on supply.

contents: The initial chemical-plus-ultrasound trial reduced stripping time, but removing the chemical without fume exhaust increased work time, manual effort, and surface damage. I ran lab and full-part trials, roughness, microscopy and SEM–EDS analysis, and documented overlap, relative-motion, and reusability risks. Normal operation stopped because cavitation erosion, particles, and reuse failed; the case produced stop gates for future scale-up.

title: Diffuser Ultrasonic Stripping Scale-up Failure and Stop Gates

contents: A model trained on public weld images lost substantial performance on practical specimens containing soot, spatter, reflections, and capture variation. I planned the overall project, compared candidate models and error images using recall and FPR, and owned low-resolution coordinate scaling and threshold FN/FP decisions. Recall on captured specimens rose from 15.84% to 85.15%, a gain of 69.31 percentage points, and the team completed a ResNet+DeiT and FastAPI/PWA inspection demo.
summary: A model trained on public weld images lost substantial performance on practical specimens containing soot, spatter, reflections, and capture variation. title: Building an AI Model to Find Defects in Welding Images

The ten-person team demonstrated Factory I/O, PLC/Ladder, SCADA/OPC UA, and web integration. DQN remained a model-selection and integration-design layer.

contents: Manufacturing, semiconductor, and battery knowledge accumulated with inconsistent terms and links, making evidence retrieval difficult. I structured the Markdown/YAML vault and link-graph index, then built a CLI that synchronizes changed files to ChromaDB and retrieves/reranks candidates. Markdown source management, incremental synchronization, candidate retrieval, and reranking are implemented. Source-location display, authorization, and repeated retrieval evaluation can extend it into an operating manufacturing-knowledge tool.

It can be extended into reproducible experiment cases by connecting notebooks, data sources, settings, and results.

contents: Exam answers, theory, and image rights come from different evidence, so fluent AI completion can create incorrect learning material. I linked questions, theory, sources, rights, and publication state and implemented learner flow and publication rules that prevent pre-submission answer exposure. The masterbook publishes only supported items and keeps conflicting or rights-uncertain material on HOLD.

The operating guide helps users find facts, documents, and official channels rather than issuing personal determinations.
